q: Checking an account balance and paying electricity bills from home through a bank's secure website is called:
x: Internet (online) banking lets customers use bank services through the bank's website or app from anywhere. ATM banking needs the customer to go to a cash machine.

q: Which medical scan uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves, with a computer building detailed pictures of the inside of the body?
x: MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) uses magnets and radio waves, and a computer turns the signals into images. A CT scan uses X-rays and ultrasound uses sound waves.

q: A company's computer calculates every employee's monthly salary, subtracts tax and other deductions and prints the pay slips. This application is a:
x: A payroll system works out wages, deductions and pay slips for staff. A point-of-sale system handles sales at a shop counter.

q: Managers in Lahore and Karachi hold a meeting in which they see and hear each other live over a network. This is:
x: Video conferencing sends live video and sound between people in different places, saving travel. E-commerce is buying and selling online, not holding meetings.

q: Data from satellites and weather stations is fed into computer models that predict tomorrow's rain and temperature. This is the use of computers in:
x: Weather forecasting runs large numbers of calculations on weather data to predict future conditions. Computer-aided manufacturing controls machines that make products.

q: A bank card that takes the money straight from the holder's own bank account at the time of payment is a:
x: A debit card draws on money already in the holder's account. A credit card lets the holder pay later, as a short loan from the bank.

q: An airline's booking computer updates its seat records the moment a seat is sold, so the same seat cannot be sold twice from offices in different cities. This is:
x: A real-time reservation system updates the central records immediately, so every office sees the current seats. Batch processing would collect bookings and process them later, allowing double sales.

q: A school designs its newsletter on a computer, arranging text, headings and photos on each page before printing. This is:
x: Desktop publishing (DTP) is the page layout of text and pictures for documents such as newsletters and brochures. CAM controls machines in a factory.

q: Hospitals keep patients' histories, test results and prescriptions on computers so that any authorised doctor can view them. These are called:
x: Electronic medical (health) records store patient information digitally for authorised staff. An expert system gives advice from stored knowledge; it is not a record store.

q: A customer uses an ATM of a different bank in another city, and the cash she takes out is deducted from her account at once. What makes this possible?
o: The card stores her balance, and the ATM updates the card
The ATM keeps a copy of every customer's account
The banks' computers are linked in a network and exchange transaction details online
The withdrawal is posted to her bank later by mail
x: The ATM sends the request over a banking network to her own bank's computer, which checks and updates her account straight away. The balance is held by the bank, not on the card or in each ATM.

q: A school's software does not teach lessons, but it records each student's test results, tracks progress and decides which lesson each student should study next. This is:
x: Computer-managed instruction (also called computer-managed learning) manages records, testing and the order of lessons. CAI is the program that actually presents the lesson and questions to the student.

q: Which job is normally done by batch processing rather than in real time?
o: Printing the monthly electricity bills of all customers together
Booking a seat on a train online
x: Monthly bills can be collected and processed all at once, with no need for an instant reply, so they suit batch processing. An autopilot, a booking or an ATM withdrawal must respond immediately.

q: The company that owns the data centres and rents out servers, storage and software over the Internet is called a:
x: A cloud service provider runs the data centres and sells cloud resources to customers. A hypervisor is software inside a server that runs virtual machines.

q: What does a school mainly need in order to use a public cloud service?
x: Public cloud services are reached over the Internet, so a connection is the main need. The provider, not the school, owns the data centre.

q: A user creates a new cloud server for herself from the provider's web page within minutes, without contacting any of the provider's staff. This cloud feature is:
x: On-demand self-service means customers can set up resources themselves whenever they need them. Multi-cloud means using services from more than one provider.

q: A cloud provider charges Rs 20 per server per hour. A shop uses 3 servers for 10 hours during a sale and then 1 server for the remaining 14 hours of the day. What is the cost for that day?
x: 3 × 10 × 20 = Rs 600 for the sale hours and 1 × 14 × 20 = Rs 280 afterwards, total Rs 880. Rs 1 440 wrongly charges 3 servers for all 24 hours; paying only for use is the point of pay-as-you-go.

q: To handle more visitors, a website adds more servers so that the load is shared among them. This is called:
x: Adding more machines to share the work is scaling out, or horizontal scaling. Scaling up means making one existing server more powerful, for example by giving it more memory.

q: Using virtualisation, a company replaces 10 lightly used physical servers with virtual machines on 2 powerful servers. What is the main benefit?
o: Each virtual machine needs its own building
Less hardware, electricity and space are needed
The programs no longer need an operating system
The company no longer needs any network
x: Combining many virtual machines on fewer physical servers (server consolidation) saves hardware, power and space. Each virtual machine still runs its own operating system.

q: A hospital is unsure about putting its patient records in a public cloud. What is its main concern?
o: Cloud storage cannot hold text files
The data would be held on servers controlled by another company
Patients' records would load too slowly to read
The public cloud would delete old records every month
x: In a public cloud the provider's staff and systems hold the data, so privacy and security of sensitive records are the worry. That is why such organisations often choose a private cloud.

q: A new company uses cloud servers instead of buying its own. What is the main money advantage?
o: It avoids a large cost for buying hardware at the start
It never has to pay anything for computing
It owns the provider's servers after one year
It needs no staff who can use computers
x: Renting cloud resources replaces a large upfront purchase with smaller payments for what is used. Cloud services are still paid for and remain the provider's property.

q: Buying a server costs Rs 120 000. Renting an equal server from a cloud provider costs Rs 5 000 per month. Ignoring all other costs, after how many months does renting cost as much as buying?
x: 120 000 ÷ 5 000 = 24 months. Before 24 months renting has cost less; after that it has cost more.

q: In Platform as a Service (PaaS), which part does the customer manage?
o: Its own application code and data
The physical servers in the data centre
The operating system of the servers
The network cables and storage disks
x: In PaaS the provider runs the hardware, operating system and run-time platform, and the customer only builds and manages its own app and data. Managing the operating system is the customer's job only in IaaS.

q: A physical server has 64 GB of RAM. The hypervisor needs 4 GB of it, and each virtual machine is given 7 GB. What is the largest number of virtual machines it can run at once?
x: 64 − 4 = 60 GB is left for virtual machines, and 60 ÷ 7 = 8 remainder 4, so 8 machines (56 GB) fit but a 9th (63 GB) does not. The answer 9 comes from forgetting the hypervisor's 4 GB (64 ÷ 7).

q: Four virtual machines run on one physical server through a hypervisor. The physical server's power supply fails. What happens?
o: The virtual machines keep running on their own
Only the hypervisor stops, not the virtual machines
x: Virtual machines are isolated from each other's software faults, but they all share the same physical hardware, so a hardware failure stops all of them. This is why important systems are spread over several physical servers.

q: A data set has 1 000 labelled images. 80% of them are used to train a model and the rest to test it. How many images are used for testing?
x: 80% of 1 000 is 800 for training, so 1 000 − 800 = 200 remain for testing. 800 is the training set, not the test set.

q: In a test of machine intelligence, a human judge chats by text with a hidden person and a hidden computer. If the judge cannot reliably tell which is the computer, it passes. This is the:
x: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing, judges whether a machine's conversation can pass for a human's. A unit test checks one small part of a program.

q: Machine learning that uses artificial neural networks with many layers, for example to recognise speech, is called:
x: Deep learning is the branch of machine learning based on many-layered neural networks. An expert system works from rules given by human experts rather than learning layers from data.

q: Many home security cameras connected to the Internet are left with their factory-set default passwords. What is the main risk?
o: The cameras will use too little electricity
Attackers may log in to watch or control the cameras
The cameras will be unable to connect to Wi-Fi
The pictures from the cameras will become blurred
x: Default passwords are widely known, so attackers can take over such IoT devices; changing the password is a basic IoT safety step. Passwords do not affect power use or picture quality.

q: The Internet of Things needs a huge number of devices, each with its own address on the network. How does IPv6 help?
o: It makes devices work without any network
It provides far more addresses than IPv4
It allows only one device per home
x: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses instead of IPv4's 32-bit ones, giving vastly more addresses for billions of devices. It does not remove the need for a network.

q: In some blockchains such as Bitcoin, computers compete to solve a hard puzzle, and the winner adds the next block and earns a reward. This is called:
x: Mining is the process of solving the puzzle (proof of work) to add and confirm a new block. Phishing is an online fraud, not part of a blockchain.

q: A chess program can beat strong players but cannot do any other task, such as translating text. This kind of AI is:
x: Narrow AI is built for one specific task. General AI would match human intelligence across many different tasks, which this program cannot do.

q: The very first block of a blockchain is called the:
x: The genesis block starts the chain and has no previous block to point to. Every later block stores the hash of the block before it.

q: Bitcoin is an example of:
x: Bitcoin is a digital currency whose transactions are recorded on a blockchain. It is not a program for searching, running a computer or sensing.

q: A model scores 99% accuracy on its training data but only 60% on new data it has not seen. What has most likely happened?
x: An overfitted model has memorised its training examples instead of learning general patterns, so it does well on them and badly on new data. An underfitted model would do poorly on the training data too.

q: Which of these is a classification task in machine learning?
o: Predicting a house's selling price in rupees
Deciding from an X-ray whether a patient has pneumonia (yes or no)
Grouping shoppers into similar groups with no labels
x: Classification puts each input into one of fixed classes, here yes or no. Predicting a price or temperature gives a number (regression), and grouping without labels is clustering, unsupervised learning.

q: A spam filter is tested on 100 e-mails: 40 are spam and 60 are not. It correctly marks 30 of the spam e-mails and 54 of the others. What is its accuracy?
x: Correct answers are 30 + 54 = 84 out of 100, so accuracy is 84%. 75% (30 of 40) and 90% (54 of 60) each count only one kind of e-mail.
